design_advice.implementation_summary: Add an integration validation pass (new EditMode test class or extension of an existing one) that opens the committed Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity scene additively (matching CommittedSceneCameraConformanceTests.cs's open/inspect/close-without-write pattern), locates representative Tilemap visuals (FloorTilemap/WallTilemap/ArchitecturalTilemap) and SpriteRenderer visuals (the WorldSpriteVisual-based Wizard and Door sprites), and asserts none of them carry a Collider, trigger, door-state, or pursuit component while the existing separately-owned gameplay objects (Floor Plane collider, WallLeft/WallRight cubes, DoorRoot's rangeTrigger/doorwayBlocker, DoorInteractable) remain the sole owners of that behavior. Pair this with a check (extending WindowsBuildSceneRegistrationTests.cs or similar) confirming the build/scene registration contains only the single canonical scene and that no SceneManager.LoadScene/LoadSceneAsync room-transition call site exists, satisfying VAL-002's continuous-scene requirement.
recommended_interfaces: Reuse DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.Build()/BuildInMemoryForTests() and existing object/component names (FloorTilemap, WallTilemap, ArchitecturalTilemap, DoorInteractable, PlayerMovement) as the inspection seam rather than introducing new production abstractions or a runtime ownership-marker API.

execution_recommendation.rationale: This is a focused integration/validation pass over an already-separated visual and gameplay layer (NSC-038/NSC-039 are delivered and integrated at HEAD, and the builder's own comments already document the ownership split). It requires moderate cross-system reasoning (Tilemap, SpriteRenderer, colliders, build settings) but follows strong existing local patterns (CommittedSceneCameraConformanceTests.cs, WindowsBuildSceneRegistrationTests.cs) rather than novel architecture. No decomposition-adjacent ambiguity or heavy refactor is expected, so standard effort is sufficient; deep reasoning is not clearly warranted and fast/mechanical would risk missing the Unity validation-agent style checks the contract requires.
